text.p: Francis Lear, who spent $25 million of a $112 million divorce settlement on a magazine named after herself, has died of breast cancer at the age of 73.
An obituary in Tuesday's New York Times said Lear, who was married for 28 years to successful TV producer Norman Lear, died at her Manhattan home on Monday.
She divorced in 1985 for an amount estimated at $112 million, which she justified because she "was very much a part of his thinking" and said, "Norman could not have done his shows without me."
Norman Lear produced the series "All in the Family" and "Maude." Frances Lear claimed she had been the inspiration for Maude, the opinionated woman played by Bea Arthur.
After the divorce she left Hollywood and moved to New York to establish Lear's, a magazine she said was aimed at women like herself "the woman who wasn't born yesterday."
She developed a reputation for being unpredictable and colleagues complained about her inexperience and capricious decisions.
A staff member wrote in a New York Times article that when Lear had been told she could not change a quotation, she shouted, "It is my magazine, and I will do what I want."

Lear worked with feminists and on political campaigns, including Eugene McCarthy's presidential campaign in 1968 and with the National Organisation for Women. She had also worked in a company that specialised in placing women executives.

Born on July 14, 1923, in a Hudson, New York, home for unwed mothers, Frances wrote in her 1992 autobiography "The Second Seduction," about her troubled childhood. She was adopted at 14 months but her adoptive father committed suicide during the Depression and a man her mother then married sexually abused her starting at age 12.
She had two brief marriages before meeting Norman Lear. She is survived by two daughters and two grandsons.
